\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Amy Gregory, Traffic Manager, reviewed the proposed resolution allowing for the installation of three traffic calming devices on Sixth Street East, near Winter Haven. She said that this meets the traffic calming policy. She said that staff recommends approval.\par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing.\par
\par
Rosa Cabrera said she supports the speed humps and requested that there are also speed humps on Avenue A. She said traffic is fast and children are next to the school. \par
\par
Rosalinda Santillan said she supports the speed humps. She said there are children playing and there is speeding. She asked for speed humps on Avenue A. \par
\par
Ms. Gregory said they did look at Avenue A and it did not meet the criteria. She will speak to Ms. Cabrera and Ms. Santillan. \par
\par
Earnest Oldaker said more of the humps should be on Avenue A instead of Sixth Street. He said they do not slow down with the speeding. He said it is the same constant vehicles speeding. \par
\par
Brittny Miller said she opposes this. She said there are a lot of trailers and said all speed humps will be in front of her house. She said there is speeding and people park on sidewalks. She said she had to walk her son in a wheelchair to school and she said to address the main issue on Avenue A. \par
\par
The Chair closed the public hearing. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said once the speed humps are installed Avenue A should be reevaluated. He said for staff to get with the Sheriff's office to do speed enforcement along Avenue A.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Sue Nelson said she is here to set the record straight. She said that the Board approved the case for Highland Club. She said it was approved based on that the roadway was to be widened to twelve foot lanes. She said she presented the Federal Highway Administration letter. She said the final scope of the project does not reflect the 12-foot lane widening to address roadway departure issues. She discussed an email between Bart Allen and Jay Jarvis. She said the funding was removed because the county was supposed to widen the lanes to twelve feet and they did not. She said not only did Mr. Jarvis misrepresent the letter, he signed off of the changes and he knows full-well why the funding was rescinded. She said Crews Lake Drive was in the CIP and would be approved as soon as Lakeland Electric relocated the utility poles. She said the land use was approved but never happened. She asked how does the county defend this. \par
\par
Kay Bourque showed slides and discussed animal control. She said shelter leadership drives the initiatives and it is the community that extends the safety net of care. She showed a model of the programs and gave an update. She asked for ordinances, support programs, and for an animal welfare advisory committee. \par
\par
Debbie Hicks said her thing today is vision. She said her vision is much brighter because the county has stepped up with animal control. She said the foundation of the facility is from 1988 and she discussed the population increase. She said she sees them opening new properties and building new facilities. She asked if some of those facilities are older than 1988. She said she sees a lot of money going into the facilities. She said we need a committee to let the community help.\par
\par
James Abercrombie said he has been in this building for 26 years. He discussed public records and said he does not understand these people. He said the text messages and anything to do with money is public record. He said he wants to see the contract that George Lindsey was involved in. He said they are responsible for him with their oath and said they are supposed to stand up for them and he needs some responses.\par
\par
County Attorney Randy Mink said we follow the public records law. He said his paralegal spoke to him and he said he was there for a public records request and if he had he made a specific request they would be happy to fulfill that. He said we fulfill them as much as we have the records and we did not refuse them. He said they will meet with Mr. Abercrombie to see what records he is needing. \par
\par
Meeting adjourned at 9:59 a.m.\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Utilities Director Tamara Richardson reviewed the resolution approving proposed revisions to the Utilities Division schedule of rates, charges, and fees. She said this increases our connection fees, makes our reclaimed irrigation rates similar to potable rates, establishes the rate for septage receiving at 15 cents a gallon, and indexes rates that came in 2024 for two more years. She recommended approval. \par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing; no one spoke. \par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Richardson said the reclaimed water used to be a disposal issue. She said reclaimed water is water after it has gone through the wastewater plant and has been treated. She said it is used for irrigation and that offsets the need of pumping out of the aquifer for irrigation. She said it is just as valuable as potable water. She said some of our areas run out of reclaimed water for irrigation and we have to supplement with potable water. She said it is more expensive to produce reclaimed water than potable water. She said there is a proposed project taking the reclaimed water to Haines City. She said it is not funded at this time because there are other projects with a higher priority. She said they got federal funding for the design of the project. She said they will do the design and they will wait until they have the money to fund that project.\par
\par
County Manager Bill Beasley stated that is a large project and they may have to do that project in phases. \par
\par
Commissioner Wilson said we have had discussions on this and he has shown his disinterest in this. He said we spend an awful lot of money on water and we have to take care of our water. He said they did not raise rates and tried to keep the costs down and then we had to raise rates because we are not in the business to lose money. He said there is a lot of discussion that can be done here and he is not for raising the rates. He said we need to look at more options.\par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Richardson said the septage receiving facility completion date is in September. She said in August/September they will start receiving the trucks to seed the plant. She confirmed there are no impact fees just connection fees for utilities. \par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Dr. Robert Weedon said he has been here before educating on humane and effective methods of Trap, Neuter, Vacinate, Return (TNVR). He discussed five people and a puppy being attacked by a rabid cat and said that represents the lack of effective management for community cats. He discussed statistics for cats taken in, euthanized, killed and the live outcome rate. He said TNVR costs less than impounding, housing, and euthanizing. He said to adopt a TNVR ordinance, fund low-cost spay and neuter, and partner with rescues and volunteers. \par
\par
Upon question, Dr. Weedon said programs will re-trap cats and vaccinate them. He said an advantage of microchipping the cats is that they have a record of vaccines. He said he was lead author on a study on response to rabies vaccines and kittens less than 12 weeks of age and they all had protective titers after vaccination. He said they know the immunity lasts longer, colony caretakers will retract the cats, and they will be boostered.\par
\par
Kay Bourque said we are here to provide a better outcome for the animals. She thanked them for hearing them, listening and beginning to make a difference. She said Animal Control is overwhelmed. She discussed a pet owner who escaped an abusive relationship and was unable to keep their pet. She discussed a stray dog that was found and puppies needing to be rescued. She said we need to focus on the source of the problem, prevent unwanted litters, and expand affordable spay and neuter. \par
\par
Aleatha Pugh speaking on behalf of Jose Antonio Palacios. She gave the Board a packet and she said that an email has been sent to Jay Jarvis regarding this property. She said Mr. Jarvis has spoken to the Town of Dundee. She requested emergency measures to address ongoing stormwater flooding affecting the Weiberg Road stormwater system since the 2020-2021 replacement of a blocked drainage pipe. She said that stormwater has continued to discharge onto private property during rain events. She discussed the impacts of the water and said measures are necessary to reduce continued impacts. She requested that Polk County and Dundee immediately evaluate and implement mitigation options. She said for both government entities to work together. She said this is within the city limits of Dundee and is off of a county owned road. She confirmed that the stormwater is handled by the county.\par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said to make an appointment to come in and discuss with the commissioners.\par
\par
Ms. Pugh said the family has made many attempts to speak to Mr. Jarvis. She said there was no response. \par
\par
Dean Meuendez said he is the founder of Dlb Cat Rescue. He said the concerns spoken do matter. He said Polk is one of the fastest growing counties and our approach to animal welfare should grow with it. He said to create partnerships with Animal Control, rescues, veterinarians, schools, businesses, and volunteers. He said together we can accomplish far more. He discussed a vision for a rescue camp. He said he is willing to work alongside and they can build something together than can serve the community and animals for generations. \par
\par
Kevin Noble said any motorcycle without a license plate on a rural road is illegal. He discussed motorcycles with no license plates. He said that ATV's are not allowed on rural roads and he said it is a safety issue. He said if they lost control the parents would be responsible for them. He said he rides his bike on the road every day. He asked them to reach out to the Sheriff's office to address this. \par
\par
County Manager Bill Beasley will discuss with the chief of staff at the Sheriff's office. \par
\par
Debbie Hicks discussed families that rescued animals. She said the public and the rescues are doing so much. She said the Sheriff's website only shows 19 dogs available and she asked why do we have so few when the kennels are full. She said they need Animal Control, a good solid facility and a committee. \par
\par
Kelly Quinn said she is asking the Board to treat animal welfare as a core county service. She said the Animal Control budget is $5.8 million while the shelter handles thousands of animals each year. She asked for a public comparison of services against other counties, investing in prevention, and evaluating whether sheltering and services should be managed through a modern civilian department while law enforcement remains coordinated with the sheriff. She said they must modernize and become more prevention focused. \par
\par
Jhoanna Allende discussed Animal Control and said we are still known as the highest kill shelter. She said we need spay and neuter vouchers, TNVR, and restricting and enforcing backyard breeders. She discussed stories of families facing difficult times with their pets. She said we need more options for people and their pets. She said the animal crisis is a huge problem and said there are too many animals entering the shelter and too many not leaving. She said all these ideas can be discussed by an animal welfare committee. \par
\par
James Abercrombie said he was here two weeks ago talking about public records. He said he cannot get straight answers or anything in writing. He discussed going to Mr. Mink's office. He said that he was told to go to the fifth floor for the records request. He said he was accused of being a liar. He said he could not have a meeting because he wanted to record it. He said he does not know what you people are trying to hide. He said we need to get a handle on this. He said has been through this for 26 years and he still cannot get it today.\par
\par
Commissioner Scott said the reason he provided hard copies was because Mr. Abercrombie said he did not receive the requests.\par
\par
Jenn Hardeman said it is disappointing to watch the Commissioners and the Sheriff's office spend time denying concerns instead of addressing them. She said the budget speaks of integrity. She said ordinance 18-68 is inconsistent and needs clarity. She said compassion is not a code violation. She said returning the cats back is not abandonment and she compared it to returning fish to a lake. She said to remember the organizational chart\par
\par
Meeting adjourned at 10:35 a.m.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 County Attorney Randy Mink reminded the audience of the DeNovo hearing procedures.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said she had ex parte communications with the applicant.\par
\par
Commissioner Wilson said he had ex parte communications with the applicant.\par
\par
Chair Santiago said she met with the applicants.\par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said he had ex parte communications with the applicant and the neighbors.\par
\par
Commissioner Scott said he met with the applicant and drove by the site. \par
\par
Ian Nance, Land Development, reviewed the request for the DeNovo hearing. He said that staff is recommending denial of the Crossed Paws Rescue Conditional Use (CU). He showed aerial photos of the site and said a codes complaint was filed stating that a dog rescue business was at this location. He stated the accessory structures were used for boarding dogs and it was found in violation of the Land Development Code (LDC). He said Residential Suburban (RS) and Agricultural Residential (AR) are the only residential uses that allows kennels. He reviewed the LDC requirements and showed properties with similar kennel uses. He discussed the site plan and said the existing kennels do not meet setback requirements. He said that the applicant has proposed that this is not open to the public for grooming and boarding services and said they will maintain records and receipts of off-site solid waste disposal. He showed photos of the site visit. He said the applicant has added fencing to help with buffers. He said the Planning Commission recommended approval 3:2 with these conditions: the kennel areas shall be fenced to ensure containment of dogs, the site is not open to the public, and a caretaker residence shall be established onsite. He said staff recommending denial stands for this hearing. He said noise is the primary issue here and there are no noise level standards applicable in RS. \par
\par
Sarah Case, applicant, showed slides and said there is a clear distinction between the ownership of the property and the Crossed Paws' operations. She said they were cited with Code Enforcement (CE) and this stemmed from a non-residential name in a residential land use. She discussed the operations, application process, and the fostering of animals. \par
\par
Erin Golotko, Vice President, Crossed Paws Pet Rescue, Inc, said the board members facilitated the funding of this property from a local non-profit because of the 501c3 and IRS compliance rules. She said they chose a property not in a dense subdivision on almost five acres that will allow for Stefanie to live onsite. She said that these are not dogs waiting to be adopted and it is their forever home. She stated no rescue operations or events will occur at this property. She discussed all the animal shelters that are helped. She said they have gone through the proper channels to come into compliance. She said this is a limited low impact use that allows a non-profit. She said this is not about expanding operations or increasing activities it is about allowing the dogs to remain in the home. She asked for the approval of this CU permit. \par
\par
Stefanie Badillo, President, Crossed Paws Pet Rescue, Inc, said she started this rescue in 2018 and has dedicated her life to rescuing dogs. She said they are not asking for county resources and they are independently funded by private donors. She said she is asking for the opportunity to continue caring for the animals by living on her property. She said their intent was to never avoid county regulations. She said the dogs on the property are chipped and registered to her. She said the dogs bark when entering the property and do not bark continuously. She said when cited by CE they started the process of bringing this into compliance. She said her idea was to live on the property with the dogs. She asked for their support and thanked them for their service.\par
\par
Ms. Case said even though the property is owned by Crossed Paws Pet Rescue, Inc, the rescue operations are held off-site. She said the dogs are owned by her and registered to her. She reviewed the land uses in the LDC regarding kennels, boarding, and breeding. She said they have to comply with the conditions listed in Chapter 303. She said focus has been on this not being a permitted use and she said this is an allowable use. She reviewed the applicant's proposed conditions of approval. She discussed similar land uses and showed maps of the proximities to residential areas for those properties. She said they are 700 feet from where the existing permitted buildings are and those will be vacated and become personal self storage. She said new kennel buildings will be moved 700 feet back. She showed the proposed site plan. She said with the conditions they can be compatible and can coexist with the neighbors. She said before them today is a land use issue.\par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Case said the structure on the SPCA site is 210 feet from a residential property line. \par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Golotko said there was a real estate professional used to purchase this property.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said this goes to understanding the use of the property. She said it is concerning that we are looking at a real estate professional suggesting that this property can be used for this.\par
\par
Ms. Case said that is where the confusion lies. She said if the property was purchased in Stefanie Badillo's name there may be complaints from the neighbors. She said Stefanie is going to live there per the conditions they have agreed to. She said they are not asking for a residential land use they are asking to allow her to keep her dogs on site and move the dogs in the three buildings 700 feet back. She said people do not come on site to visit or adopt and there are not any events on site. \par
\par
Ms. Golotko stated there is a large community of fosters and the dogs do not come onto the property. She said she finds a foster and calls them after they leave the vet. She said she does not bring them to this property.\par
\par
Upon question, Mr. Nance said there is no limit within the LDC for the number of dogs they can keep on site. He said it is the accessory structures being used for housing the dogs that is the factor. He said to construct a building for personal dogs you would not have to come in as an individual and apply for kennel operations. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott asked how is this a kennel operation when there is no use of commercial operations and the dogs are registered in her name. \par
\par
Mr. Nance responded and said he does not believe the owner lives there at this time. He said there are vaccination records that would lead staff to believe it is a non-residential use. He said there are receipts of dumping waste and it is not normal for pet ownership to take large amounts of waste to be dumped.\par
\par
Ms. Golotko said they keep the records if Animal Control were to show up. She said they get fined if they do not have all the information. She said for the waste they do it as a courtesy to the neighbors and they do not want all the waste on the property. \par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said with that statement she is extremely confused because they are saying that these dogs are her personal dogs, but now they are telling them they keep the records should they be turned over to somebody else. \par
\par
Ms. Golotko said Animal Control has been called multiple times to the property and they have it ready to show if they have questions. She said the dogs are not being turned over it is for the authorities if they have questions. \par
\par
Ms. Badillo said Animal Control requires them to have the tags and the rabies certificates. She said they want to make sure the animals are taken care of and they want a picture of every rabies tag. She said all the dogs on the property are hers and she has not brought any new dogs to the property.\par
\par
Ms. Case said CE was called for 50 kennels onsite and dogs barking. She said staff replied with an email that there has already been a case opened for this. She said they were reported for noise and CE reported that there were no dogs on site and saw there were buildings under construction. She said CE got a call four months before the dogs were moved on site.\par
\par
Mr. Mink said this is not for the CE case. He reminded the Board that this is a land use case involving whether or not a kennel is a consistent and compatible use for this location. He said they can confirm whether they heard noise.\par
\par
Tonya Long, Codes Investigation Supervisor, said the complaint was for an advertisement of fundraiser activities. She said they did not find that the dogs had come in until July and that was when the noise complaint started. She stated that was when they started meeting with neighbors and they were cited after the July date. She said in March they did meet with them to let them know that this would be a requirement before moving the dogs on site and they still did it without the approvals. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said there is no limit of dogs on an individuals property. He said that is something this Board needs to remedy in the near future. He said with looking at other counties we have the ability to regulate that and we probably should. \par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Long said dogs barking is handled under the Animal Control Ordinance. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said it can also be enforced through the Noise Control Ordinance through the Sheriff's office.\par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Case said they are not disputing a CE active case and CE said the proper channel would be to get a Level 3 CU for a kennel. She said the owners are refuting that they are a kennel because they are so different from the SPCA and the Bully Project. She said they are trying to come in compliance and are trying to be good neighbors. She confirmed that there are no adoptions and the family feeds the dogs and that is the coming and going. She said there are private donors providing funds. She discussed what the owner does so the dogs are not euthanized.\par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Golotko discussed the board that oversees this. She said there is open communication with the members and said she oversees the financial aspects. She said only dogs that are owned by the property owner are on the property. She said there is another property where the adoptions take place. \par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Badillo said all dogs would be registered to her. She said she does not bring new dogs onto the property.\par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Golotko said it is a requirement for a board through the IRS because it is a 501c3. She said they stopped construction on the house and the house was not able to be lived in at the time of purchase. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said boards are for commercial operations where people make decisions. \par
\par
Ms. Golotko said they do adoptions that are off site and that is what the board is for. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott discussed how you cannot funnel money out of a non-profit into a personal name to take care of personal business. He said a simpler path is an individual name without the 501c3.\par
\par
Ms. Golotko said they spoke to an attorney and that was not an option because of the code violation and the neighbors. She said the problem would not go away had they changed the name.\par
\par
Ms. Case reiterated that these are her personal dogs that are all registered to her. She said they are asking for permission for their personal dogs. She said they want to build a new building 700 feet away and Sefanie wants to live there with her dogs. She said no rescue operations are on site and this will be the homestead once built. She said they are here for a land use matter. \par
\par
Garry Bozeman, appellant, said he lives next to the property. He said their website says it is a rehabilitation center and this is a pit stop until they are adopted. He said the barking is constant and the smell is horrendous. He said he does not know what they are doing with the animal waste and whether it is being washed out. He said what they are doing is good but not in a residential neighborhood. He said there is barking six to eight hours a day seven days a week. He said dogs are brought there to rehabilitate and they have an office off site. He said it states it is a pit stop for the dogs.\par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing. \par
\par
Angel Sims said years ago she was looking for a mom and pop rescue and she came across Crossed Paws. She said the site visits and drop-offs are no more than the average family. She said she has honked her horn and has not heard dogs barking. She said something needs to be looked at on how rescues are handled in the county. She said to vote in favor. She said this is a place with the animals indoors and the animals are taken out in shifts. She said it is a wide open area and is a decent fit for a project like this.\par
\par
Steve Everett said he is a lifelong resident of Auburndale. He said he needs more than three minutes and he asked if they can get in trouble for lying up here. He said the rally filled up the whole place trying to get donations. He said he saw dogs going in and out. He said it is still right next to his property. He discussed the smell of dog feces. He asked if they would like to listen to this 24/7. He said this is a business she makes money off of and they have lied. He asked if any of them would like to put up with this for the rest of their life. He said it is a weed and it should not be there. He said she picked the wrong place. He said all the questions they answered they lied.\par
\par
Marian Bozeman said she has built her life there. She said she has never experienced as much stress since Crossed Paws arrived. She said she has a koi pond and garden and she cannot tend to it without noise. She said she walks in fear that a dog could escape and confront her. She said after she filed a complaint cameras were installed and were pointed to her property. She said she was approached in her yard alone and she said this is bullying and harassing. She asked how can the county allow this to continue. She said this is a safety concern and this operation will only grow larger. She said at her age she should be able to live peacefully.\par
\par
Ruth Krischick said she is speaking on behalf of Crossed Paws. She said she has been a volunteer and adopter. She said the team is professional and is committed to the animals. She discussed the operations of the rescue and thanked them for doing a good job with the animals. \par
\par
Linda Bayko said she is in support of Crossed Paws. She said it has been a meaningful difference with rescuing over 200 dogs each year. She said it provides a temporary shelter and provides food. She asked for the approval to be upheld and for them to continue their work. She discussed a music machine to help keep the dogs from barking and said she has a hard time believing there is any barking going on. \par
\par
Mary Lou Hammond said she is a huge animal lover and has known Stefanie for three years. She said the dogs on the property are her dogs. She said nobody else wanted the dogs and she takes care of her dogs. She said that she is exceptional.\par
\par
The Chair closed the public hearing.\par
\par
Commissioner Scott said he went on the Crossed Paws website and watched the YouTube video posted. He said it talks about how this is just a pit stop for dogs. He said the title is Crossed Paws Rescue Rehabilitation Center in Auburndale. He said he would like to know why this is portrayed as the dogs trying to find their forever home. He said he expects clarity on what information they are being provided and for this video to portray that these dogs are at the facility in Auburndale waiting for their forever home contradicts the testimony given today. \par
\par
Ms. Badillo said the video was put up and they had not been cited by the county. She said she thought they were doing everything by the book and after they were cited she did not bring any new dogs. She said she is taking the video down and did not know it was still up. She said everything that has been spoken is the truth. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said it directly contradicts everything that has been given today. He said he can tell by the structural photos with dogs they are talking from July 2025.\par
\par
Ms. Badillo confirmed that she is on the Board of Directors, they report to the IRS as a 501c3, and the board is active.\par
\par
Ms. Case said they did show her that the video was active and she was hoping that it was not active. She said the intent was to find property and have an active rescue. She said they know they cannot do anything she is advertising on the website. She said with the substantial evidence they heard from her today regarding the land use issue and the conditions of approval that would be the pathway to enforce this. She said the compatibility was mitigated with the distance and the extra measures proposed with the new buildings. She asked for the appeal to be denied and to uphold the Planning Commission's recommendation of approval. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said he is not in favor of this operation from a land use standpoint, noise and odor. \par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said this case has been challenging as she considered the facts. She said the decision is based on land use and regulations. She read the definition of compatibility. She said often times they are looking at density, activity, and lot sizes. She stated with this case they look at and consider the negative impacts. She said this case does not stop anyway what Crossed Paws does because this has nothing to do with the rescue and they were told these are personal animals. She said we are not here to talk about compassion or animal welfare we are here to talk about land use. She said when she looks at the definition of compatibility she does believe there is harm. She said she does not believe this will be a stable situation overtime. She said as much as she would love to see a pet rescue place she does not believe this is the place for a kennel. She said if this is her personal home and she lives there that is another route the parties will have to decide. She said when we look at the land use a kennel run by anyone is not the appropriate place. \par
\par
Chair Santiago said she is looking at this as a land use case also. She said if they meet the conditions set by the Planning Commission then she is in favor of this. She said she is looking at if the conditions have been met. She said we need to do something for the animals in Polk County. She said if these animals were not in the kennels they would be roaming and they would have another issue. She said if someone does not do it, who will. She said this is a project that is helping the people and she likes to see there are donors helping and that is her personal opinion.\par
\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Commissioner Scott said he has a resolution he would like to propose with CareerSource. He stated he had some concerns on some of the data he was seeing off the Florida CareerSource dashboard for their ranking and how we are doing performance wise. He said we received a letter from the state that has brought the county into some responsibilities. \par
\par
County Attorney Randy Mink said that they received a letter from CareerSource Florida which laid out several issues and concerns they had. He said this supports a temporary removal to allow the Board to have a governance review of CareerSource Polk. He said what is being proposed is the temporary removal of the executive director until reinstated by this Board to allow for the governance review. He said it states that she shall be treated as not being permanently removed until reinstated by the Board and not to have any access to the buildings, offices, computer programs, computers, and emails. He said the Board asked him to look at the contract and it is with the CareerSource Polk Board and it does provide 52 weeks of severance pay. He said her current salary is around $220,000. He said that will be subject to litigation if we get into litigation. He confirmed that the severance pay is without cause termination and he said there are specific clauses listed in their agreement about being convicted of a felony and a willful neglect of duties. He said that is between them, the Board, and Polk County as the chief elected official has the authority under statute to remove the executive director of the board with cause. He said they will have a recommendation to CareerSource for an interim director.\par
\par
Vice Chair Braswell said this is a convoluted mess when an organization is a non-profit that we oversee the director but we do not pay the director and we do not have a contract with the director. He said however this turns out they need to re-visit this with CareerSource Florida and asked if this the best way to be operated. He said he has been questioning Indeed and Monster that do the same thing. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said that will come out in the governance process for whatever changes with the relationship with CareerSource Polk. He said they can look at things they can change to prevent this from occurring in the future. He said the Board could be involved more before they get to a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said when he initially came on the board and when you go into a PIP it is there for a reason. He stated there are metrics they are held to. He said when you look at the data we rank last and that is not our standard. He said the CareerSource Florida letter states that the CEO had an opportunity to present herself at a meeting and declined. He said when you are on a PIP and decline a meeting that is significant disregard for what the organization could do. He said he looks forward to the governance review.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said this letter is public record. She said to get a letter from a state agency that says, "alarmingly we have noted a trend of non-cooperation, questionable fiscal management, and in some cases outright deception by the president and it names her". She said the people of Polk deserve better, the amount of tax dollars that are available for workforce training and to have somebody who is involved in an improvement plan going back to March 2026 and then to violate that improvement plan and not show up that defines a willful failure to perform job duties. \par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Chair Santiago opened a public hearing. \par

Emily Hils addressed the Board concerning Flock cameras. She said she is asking the Board to work with Sheriff Judd on the removal of Flock cameras. She discussed the Sheriff's continued hostility to voluntarily remove the cameras and asked that the Board cut funding within the sheriff's budget where Flock funding resides. She discussed her public records requests from the Sheriff's office. She said FDOT confirmed that the Sheriff's office has requested 42 cameras installed between 2023 and 2025. She discussed the lack of transparency and said they opted not to engage in a transparency portal. She discussed two-factor authentication to prevent password sharing and limits for users to choose who has access to the community's data. She reviewed the information binder that she has submitted to the Board. She said Flock cameras are becoming a political poison pill. She discussed Flock's vision to eliminate all crime in America. She said they should instead focus on the mix of biological, psychological, social, and economic factors that contribute to crime. She discussed the camera system in China. She said surveillance is a symptom of an angry, disempowered, and untrusting society wants armed forces and police to solve problems. She said the last time she can remember a private company selling communities on an impossible pipe dream at the expense of our safety is when the Sackler family introduced their actual poison pill. She said if the sheriff will not voluntarily protect our right to privacy or our location data it is up to the Board to do it for us. \par
\par
Dawson Bowman said he would like to address the Board concerning Flock cameras and said he is against all of these cameras. He said these cameras are being used because they are accessible by any means. He discussed a Haines City police officer accessing these cameras for personal use illegally. He said the extent of information collected is invasive. He discussed how cars are tracked. He said he does not like the behavior and attitude of Flock as a company; he said they publicly lie often. He said they have reinstalled cameras after they were asked to remove them. He said they are too easily accessible and there are 50 plus known vulnerabilities. He said he would also like to express his disapproval of data centers. \par
\par
Magdeline Dupery expressed her concerns on the amount of funding that is being put towards AI surveillance technology. She discussed the types of recognitions these cameras collect. She discussed the lack of input from the community. She said the Commissioners complain about signs in the right-of-way and discussed the dangers of the Flock cameras in the right-of-way. She said it changes the way they think about crimes. She said this is pre-crime monitoring. She asked they cut the budget for these specific tools. \par
\par
Sam Romaine said Sheriff Judd has said that these types of readers help to solve crimes and find missing people. He said he is not sure why they should trust the best sheriff in American when you can trust somebody in the Facebook comments who has watched a video on the subject. He said there are no excuses for what happened in Haines City and the officer who accessed the Flock cameras illegally. He said this should not cost honest officers from using this type of technology. He said there should be enforceable limits. He said government surveillance should have enforceable limits required, legitimate purpose for searches, restrict the sharing of data, delete routine records promptly, audit the access, and public compliance records. \par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Linnes Finney, representing Stacy-Campbell-Domineck, said the resolution terminates Ms. Campbell-Domineck before they have heard anything from her. He said the county is taking an extraordinary step of removing a sitting president and CEO based on an asserted cause theory. He said there are three points the commission must keep and focus on the governing contract. He said her employment is governed by a CEO contract from July 2024 - July 2029. He said the contract permits immediate cancellation for cause only for willful failure to perform duties after 30 days of written notice, conviction of a felony crime, or arrest for indictment for a breach of trust crimes such as embezzlement, fraud or perjury. He said there is no proof of any of these. He said the county sites neglect of duty, gross mismanagement and lack of performance. He said it is their position that these labels do not override the contract. He said the contract requires 30 days written notice and an opportunity to cure any alleged willful failure to perform. He said these are conclusions and are not facts or evidence. He said the process has been unfair and prejudicial. He said on July 31, 2026, the BoCC held public discussion and he discussed the concerns that were raised. He read a formal response document into the record. He reviewed her board evaluations by CareerSource Polk and said the most recent performance review meets and exceeds expectations and that is not the profile of someone who should be permanently removed. He said they are asking them to apply the correct standard, insist on specificity and proof, and recognize the contract for cause requirements have not been met. He said they are asking them to recognize that the county's materials reflect disputes, unresolved factual questions, and to acknowledge evidentiary gaps. \par
\par
Ms. Campbell-Domineck was sworn in by County Attorney Randy Mink. \par
\par
Ms. Campbell-Domineck responded to questions from Mr. Finney and stated her name for the record. She said she was the president and CEO of CareerSource Polk and has worked at CareerSource since 2002. She said after working there for four years she was encouraged to apply as CEO, was interviewed and selected in 2006. She described the mission and goal of CareerSource Polk. She discussed her primary role as CEO. She said she is a member of the Florida Workforce Development Association, a number of boards with Lakeland Regional Health, the ALPI, and the Citizens Healthcare Oversight Committee (CHOC). She said she is not sure why she was removed from the CHOC. She discussed the organizations CareerSource partners with. She said her employment agreement is governed by a written agreement and it defines what for cause termination means. She said she has not been convicted of a felony, arrested or indicted for a breach of trust crime, was not given a 30-day written notice, and did not refuse to perform her duties. She said she has not read in the report from Canopy that there was gross mismanagement. She said there has not been any evidence of lack of performance or non-cooperation. She said she has not abandoned her role. She discussed the CareerSource Polk board members and the requirements to be on the board. She said she is reviewed annually by CareerSource Polk and she discussed the performance evaluation and their HR process. She discussed how the members are selected and she confirmed that the BoCC approved the members. She discussed her 2024-2025 evaluation and said that her evaluation made her feel great. \par
\par
Mr. Finney reviewed some of the comments from the CareerSource Polk members on her evaluation.\par
\par
Ms. Campbell-Domineck said there were no findings in the last audit. She said the last negative audit finding was maybe over 15 years ago. She said after her removal on September 1, 2026, she had no access to anything, no pay and no benefits. She said she completed the investigative form and her benefits would end on September 30 and there were no options for COBRA or extending her benefits. She said she did not have access to necessary information to respond to the correspondence. She said she was told to reach out to Nilda Blanco to get information. She said that there is information in her e-mails she would have used for responses. She confirmed that there is an allegation that she began training on things that had not been approved. She discussed the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). She said the state has a policy and if they want to create local operating procedures it has to align with what the policy allows. She said the CDL agreements expired June 30th and they did not remove them. She said they did not renew because she had been working with a colleague to understand their best practice of not having agreements with training providers. She said the state is responsible for approving all training providers and she said a local board does not have to approve training providers. She said customers can go to the state list. She said their annual meeting is unique and has been in place since 1996 and the Men of the Workforce event was a campaign. She discussed this campaign and said the goal was to raise funds for workforce incentives. She said $31,220 was raised, 30 cars were given away and they cannot use workforce funds She said no participant lost services, benefits, opportunities or eligibility based on sex or any other protected characteristic. She said that it did not violate WIOA. She discussed office closings and said it was posted that it was closed but the challenge was that it was not on a schedule of operations. She responded to questions from Mr. Finney regarding no children allowed signs. She said that the record does not show intentional misconduct, fraud, personal gain, discrimination or harm. She asked if they have documentation outside of what has been provided that warrants removal for cause that it is provided and they have the same opportunity to dispute it. She said based on the allegations and the things they have discussed it would not warrant termination for cause. \par
\par
Upon question, Ms. Campbell-Domineck said that Luz Heredia is the HR director for Career Source. She said it is a part-time position and they report to her. \par
\par
Adil Khan responded to questions from Mr. Finney. He discussed the boards he has served on and his professional role. He discussed Ms. Campbell-Domineck and said she was good at communication and prepping before meetings. He said that she was always on top of everything. He said there were never any fiscal problems and said they had stellar audits. He discussed her leadership and said her experience is exemplary. He discussed the donated money she collected and said she had great ideas. He said the evaluation is anonymous for all 15 people and all of them rating her the same tells you a lot. He responded to questions to the four allegations against Ms. Campbell-Domineck and confirmed that they do not have intentional wrongdoing, fraud, personal gain, misuse, or willful misconduct. He discussed the award he created in 2022 to reward staff members. He discussed the annual meetings. He said the Men of the Workforce has to have champions and fundraising. He said it was inappropriate to deny access to office equipment and records. He said she goes above and beyond the call of duty and he discussed her involvement in the community. He said they help people get jobs. \par
\par
Mr. Finney discussed and submitted letters of support into the record. He had final comments and asked them to vote no on the termination of Ms. Campbell-Domineck. \par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing.\par
\par
Gary Clark said CareerSource Polk has diligently supported this community for decades. He said they have been the sponsors for best places to work since 2003. He said throughout this investigative process they have not been given the opportunity to address the Board. He requested for any issues or problems for them to provide specifics. He said as volunteers they give many hours, are proud of their work and continue to be advocates for improving access to jobs.\par
\par
Reverend William Boss spoke in support of Ms. Campbell-Domineck. He said he saw leadership and diversity. He said misinformation has been developed. He asked them to not remove her from her position. He said they do not want to go home today knowing with what was presented today that there was nothing unethical or illegal. He discussed her not having medical benefits. \par
\par
Katrina Lunsford said when management and organizations work together you probably will not end up this way. She said when they had problems before there was a liaison with monthly meetings. She discussed the price that is paid for standing up. She said it took a lot to fight to get before them today and she has never seen where they had to fight to say hello to each other. She asked if there is something within the county that needs to be tweaked for employees and operations. \par
\par
Mr. Finney submitted the 24/25 performance evaluation and responses to the July 31st meeting.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said everything Mr. Finney just submitted they had for some time and it is not new information. \par
\par
Ms. Lunsford said when we had problems before they had the county manager and county attorney communicate before they got excited in this room. She said looking at the operational side would cause less stress when making decisions. \par
\par
The Chair closed the public hearing. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said the quarterly meetings have not occurred for a while. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said he does not like how this has all come down. He said we do not oversee CareerSource Polk and he asked if there is an ongoing investigation. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said Canopy is still collecting information and they will assist the Board. He said in December there will be a report on what CareerSource Polk needs to be doing.\par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said he still feels rushed and he does not know if we have all the facts. He said he is not in favor of termination with cause because he does not think cause has been established. He said it is a non-profit that is funded or sponsored by the state with federal money that flows to CareerSource. He said the State has determined they do not have confidence in CareerSource Polk. He said it might be appropriate to reset CareerSource Polk and start all over again. He said if she is terminated he does not believe it should be with cause and to let her contract play out. He said the state wants change and there will be change whether we do it or don't. He said it is not fair to do it with cause but there needs to be a reset.\par
\par
Commissioner Scott said the 17th and 21st place is from letter grades and performance. He discussed the latest report and said dating back to 2022 it is either last place or 17th place. He said going back to 2022 there is a higher score and from 2023-2024 you see the downward trend. He said there are letter grades that come out each year and he said there are updates annually. He said the data comes from CareerSource Florida and it is numerical data. He said the 15 board members provide feedback and he did not hear there was feedback from anybody who works with the CEO and the organization. He said the health of the organization is not just the board members that are volunteer based and attends meetings it is the ones that walk the office halls and sit in the seats. He said the future board should incorporate CEO reviews. He said his opinion is not that this is a horrible organization or that it has failed 100% of the time; he said it is his opinion that it has slipped significantly over the last several years and it has not had a course of rebound nor had the leadership to get it where it could go. He said there are a lot of people in the county that need to get a job and training. He said specific to his company they tried a couple times and the third time they gave up and blamed it on themselves. He stated based on his experience as an employer in the county he did not have success with it. He did not say it was horrible then and he did not go on and bash them. He said in June 2025 the Winter Haven facility closed and online it lists the Lakeland center for all services and from a leadership perspective there are hundreds of thousands of dollars that should have been able to keep open a Winter Haven center or find another center without having to come to Lakeland. He said the PIP is a written notice that has metrics that need to be met. He said there are ways to educate ourselves, learn new stuff and improve and that would be beneficial to CareerSource Polk. He said the PIP provided a 30-day written notice and to still have lack of performance and leadership. He said the analytics don't show an organization that just started to slip. He spent a year and a half evaluating and then they got the letter from the state of the obligations they had as a county. He said we had a timeline and they were not willing to extend it and there have been years of it getting to where it is now. He discussed 126 people being served for three quarters in a row. He said there is stuff beyond that to make the resources great and make it serve the community. \par
\par
Commissioner Wilson said he was not involved in CareerSource Polk. He said we got a letter from the state telling them what they need to do and how little time they have to do something. He said we have never had nor want any control over this and it has been in their court. He said we have spent time and tax payers' money on this. He said the state is going to do something and we will do something. He said there are some things that will happen, we did not ask for this, but we will handle this. \par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said she has poured hours into deciphering this. She said in August 2025 the Board and CareerSource Polk was notified of the issue and this is not new and we have to take ownership that we were not aware of our oversight responsibilities and that is why it feels rushed. She said when placed on a PIP technical assistance has already tried and failed; she said that is notice that the job is not being performed satisfactorily. She said saying they don't have factual information you can easily go to CareerSource Florida and click on the letter grades for scoring. She said they were performing well until 2022 when we saw significant changes. She reviewed the decreases in performance. She said the CEO is evaluated on the federal performance requirements and the 18 performance measures are included in this report and it is a clear understanding on how they are being graded. She said they look at economics of the local workforce and population and with the federal and state information there is an agreed upon adjusted goal and we are failing to meet that goal. She said to say that we need to see failures in all areas is short selling this county. She discussed the current bylaws and she asked where is the member from Polk State College and the public schools. She asked where are the bylaws and she said the minutes of their meetings do not match the bylaws that are available to the public. She said the minutes for the meeting say there was action taken by a person who was marked absent. She said she does not know if they do not know how to take notes or keep records or if there is deception. She said there is great concern when she looks over this. She directed them to look at their bylaws where the superintendent of Polk County Public Schools and the president of Polk State College shall have permanent appointments and they are not on that board. She said the bylaws and the minutes do not match and she said we cannot operate like that as a government entity. She said the piece that is missing in the performance evaluation is what is CareerSource Polk responsible for and that is for jobs for people of Polk County. She said nowhere do they look at the metrics that come out of the report and is it factored into her evaluation. She said the ultimate responsibility is about meeting those 18 standards and we have failed to meet them year after year starting in 2022. She asked how long do we need this to go on. She said according to policies we are eligible for sanctions and those sanctions may end up being merged into another workforce board. She said that will be detrimental to the workforce and the economy of Polk County. She said to think our workforce training and development may be combined with another county is alarming or they may select an alternative entity to administer our workforce training. She said it appears we have failed a couple of federal standards three years in a row. She said the facts are we are not performing as CareerSource Polk. She said it is time for a reset and she does believe there is cause. She stated every standard on how this was measured has not been carried out. She said we have been on a downward trend since 2022, we need a change, and the people of Polk deserve better. She said there is a tremendous amount of money going into this. She said many children and families do not have the luxury to go off to college and come back and get a job; she said our action today can severely impact the ability of our residents to be able to stay in this county and get training for any job they want. \par
\par
Chair Santiago said in July when Commissioner Scott brought this to their attention they were all surprised with the bottom standing. She said they did say to move forward with an investigation and she did not expect that at the next meeting they would have the removal of Ms. Campbell-Domineck. She thought they would go through some processes and meetings. She said she will not support the removal of Ms. Campbell-Domineck because we are not there and there is convoluted information. She said we need to move forward with more conversations and information. She said Stacy has been in this position for a long time and we owe her an opportunity to share how this can be corrected but that has not happened. She said she is not going to support this resolution for permanent removal. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott confirmed that we have spent $195,000 in taxpayers' money to respond to the state's letter. He said Ms. Campbell-Domineck was very good during meetings rationalizing what is in the PIP, that it is more administrative in nature, and that it was not that serious. He said it was not lets have an emergency meeting or establish procedures; it was we did not fill out some paperwork and there is reporting that was not what the state wanted. He said one of the board members mentioned that with the office closures he would approve them based on the recommendations of the CEO. He said he can understand that because Ms. Campbell-Domineck was good at pitching that everything was great. He said he wished he did not take it at face value. He said there was also a statement made that there were no negative audit findings in years. He said in September 2025 there were 11 findings, 6 non-compliance issues, and 4 repeat findings. He discussed CDL programs and said Gulf Coast has been last since 2023 and we mirrored a program that has been last. He said over the last four years there has been a slide and the unwillingness to correct. He said we can be 1, 2, or 3 but it is going to take proper leadership and a board. He said we have a lot to improve.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman discussed the monitoring report in 2023/2024 and said there were 7 findings and she read from those findings. She said year after year we are seeing these issues. She said this is not being rushed we were just not in the discussions. She said it is the responsibility to reset this board to align with workforce development. She said we got in the conversation when the state called our attention to it and she is embarrassed to say that. She said before the PIP there was corrective action that involved technical assistance. \par
\par
Commissioner Wilson said Polk is out $200,000 and CareerSource has money in their bank and we need to be reimbursed. He said we are the ones who got the letter, who are trying to figure out what is going on and it is costing the taxpayers money. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said he brought this up in July before the state sent the letter. He said if you sit in the meetings and read the minutes it does not come across as this is all fixing to crumble. He said ownership was put on the county to hire a consultant. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said the county is not subject to the contract and the statute does not provide a severance clause. He said that does not come into factor from our perspective. He said we are working under the statute and there is no severance provided and that is the position of the county. \par
\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 County Manager Bill Beasley discussed the 2026-2027 Final Budget for the Polk County Workforce Development Board d/b/a CareerSource Polk. \par
\par
Nilda Blanco, Interim Director CareerSource Polk, showed slides and gave an overview of the final budget. She said funds are allocated from the state. She said the programs support individuals that meet various criteria for participation. She discussed the participation criteria. She said the preliminary budget of $9.54 million was approved by CareerSource, the state and the Board. She said the final budget increased $736,943 and the final budget is $10,274,216. She said the budget supports job search assistance, career planning, occupational skills training, work-based learning, youth programming, summer employment and organizational management and governance. \par
\par
Mr. Beasley said that these are 100% federal funds and are passed directly through CareerSource Polk through Florida Commerce and has no effect on the county budget. He recommended approval. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said it is odd that we are in the process. He said it is federal money that comes through the state and we do not have anything to do with this. He stated they have a board of directors that approves the budget and he asked why are we involved in this. \par
\par
County Attorney Randy Mink said the state statute requires this and is a part of the oversight. \par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said the oversight part is what got us here in the first place. \par
\par
Mr. Mink confirmed that the liaison does not vote. \par
\par
Ms. Blanco said it is set out in WIOA through statute and she said it is the Board's responsibility to appoint a board and the accountability comes back to the Commission. She said the local elected officials have the opportunity to make sure the dollars were spent appropriately and that they are addressing the workforce demands of accounting. She said they are required to work with other strategic partners and with Polk State there are different programs they would want to connect through. She said with performance metrics they make sure individuals are increasing their skills, gaining credentials, and going to work. She said they are also evaluated on making sure that displaced individuals are able to get a job. \par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said the mess is reflective of a lack of engagement. She said the vision going forward is communication, changes, fluctuations and having scheduling events together. She said Ms. Blanco was put in touch with somebody from Mosaic and they already have a plan of when they are going to do a career fair. She said the vision of CareerSource Polk and other workforce boards is more than dislocated workers and how can we work on and improve our workforce. She said it takes all the various partners from the K-12 system, Polk State, and private colleges to have a robust workforce we need a variety of providers. She said community members have expressed that there has not been involvement from CareerSource Polk and she has had some people in economic development tell her that their phone call has gone unanswered for three years. She said our disconnect from the process and the previous CEO not connecting as well with the community has led us to where we are. \par
\par
Ms. Blanco confirmed that a report will be given to the Board.\par
}
title: Approve the 2026-2027 Final Budget for the Polk County Workforce Development Board d/b/a CareerSource Polk

He said this is in conjunction with a subdistrict change and a modification to a solid waste management facility Conditional Use (CU). He said that the Planning Commission and staff recommends approval of transmittal. \par
\par
Upon question, Mr. Ziskal said that the CU will be back before the Board in December with the land use change and the subdistrict change. He reviewed the site plan map. He said there will be four access sites for the recycling operation. \par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing.\par
\par
Whitney Richie said there has been a population increase of over 100 people in 2026. She said these agriculture and rural lifestyles have been maintained for decades. She said Bradley Junction residents will be close to the landfill with odors, dust, noise, biomaterials and chemicals. She said one side will have a chemical plant and the other side will have the biohazard recycling facility. She spoke in opposition and said to protect the citizens. \par
\par
Henrietta Pettys said her husband bought his house in 1998. She said they love living out there with all the wildlife. She discussed the increased traffic. She said that they like it peaceful.\par
\par
Bryan Lynch said he lives in Mulberry and close to Bradley Junction. He said he does not want a landfill. He asked the Board if they would want a landfill in their community. He asked why he cannot drink his well water safely; he said he does not want to contaminate himself. He said the ground water is historically contaminated. He said this is our land and they want to put this in our land. He asked what are we dumping on this for and he said to take pride in our nation.\par
\par
Sharon Ford said this is unfair. She said everything is going down and they do not have street lights. She said this will make things worse and their property value will go down. She said this is not healthy and she is opposed to this. \par
\par
Tom Mims, applicant, responded to public comment. He said there is a misunderstanding, they are referring to a landfill, and the landfill is already permitted and approved by the county. He said this has nothing to do with a landfill and the landfill is already there. He referred to the map and said it is recycling and is part of the landfill operation. He said around 2010, the county imposed strict operations on recycling within heavy industrial land uses. He said if you want a recycling operation it is limited to Institutional land uses not Industrial. He said the purpose is to establish more recycling operations and not to expand the landfill. \par
\par
The Chair closed the public hearing. \par
\par
Upon question, Mr. Ziskal said this it to transmit to Florida Commerce for their review. He said this will come back to the Board on December 15th for this land use change, a change from Institutional 1 to Institutional 2, and a modification to the CU. He said the CU provides the parameter for site operations with the buffers, intensities and types of uses. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said the CU is not automatic and there is another step before such a use would be allowed. \par
\par
Commissioner Scott said when you talk about recycling and he referred to BS Ranch. He said there is a stigma to the topic of organic matters with odors and mismanagement practices. He said to give an assurance that will not be in their back yard.\par
\par
Mr. Ziskal said the CU provides control for the odor, enclosures, buffering and noise.\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 County Manager Bill Beasley discussed the permanent closure of the Northeast Landfill Temporary Residential Customer Convenience Center, Pilot Project, effective January 1, 2027. \par
\par
Waste and Recycling Director Brian Cogswell showed slides and discussed the services that were provided with the convenience center that was opened for illegal dumping. He showed a map of where illegal dump sites were investigated and cleaned up. He said the total number of customers was the same month over month. He said the repeat customers grew dramatically and they anticipated that was from commercial customers using this to supplement their businesses at a reduced rate. He discussed illegal dumping statistics and said the average was 22 vehicles per day with about 7 tons per day collected. He said revenue was around $9,000 - $11,000 per month and the average cost is around $40,000 a month and they are having to supplement about $30,000 a month. He said they reduced the manpower to reduce some of the supplementation. He said it comes out to a net loss of $357,000 if they continue through the end of the year. He recommended discontinuing the project on 1/1/2027 and having a mass media campaign. He said they will search for alternative prevention strategies. He said they will promote enforcement with the Sheriff's office and Code Enforcement. He said there are possible Land Development Code amendments for the standards of multi-family sites. \par
\par
Upon question, Mr. Cogswell said the garbage truck drivers report illegal dumping. He said Code Enforcement does self initiated reporting and citizens call in. He said Code Enforcement investigates and then sends it to them. He said if something is found on the side of the road those sites grow and grow and said a claw truck is sent out for every dump site that has been reported the previous week. He said they had hundreds of users there 1-4 times and they have a few that have been there 40-60 times and that is not consistent with residential usage. He said customers have been turned away from coming from another county or they were identified as commercial. He said closing by January 1st they will reduce the loss by $150,000. He said by reducing the staffing they saved $75,000 and this would be an additional savings. He said he has the capacity in their budget to increase the claw truck to two days a week. \par
\par
Chair Santiago said this is not the data she wanted to hear. She said she does not understand how or why somebody would do that to our county. She said the problem is throughout the county. She said she is sorry to see this closing and she hoped that this would have been a solution. She said we need to move forward and not continue wasting taxpayers' money. She said the media campaign is going to be important in notifying people. She said for the people to help stop the illegal dumping so our county is beautiful throughout. She thanked the commission and said she is sorry to see this closing. \par
\par
Mr. Beasley recommended approval of closing this pilot project effective January 1, 2027.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Land Development Director Ben Ziskal reviewed the proposed Compatibility text amendment. He said that staff and the Planning Commission recommends approval. He said this is a first reading and no action is required.\par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said if a developer brings in something that staff does not think complies then they will be able to negotiate with the county on whether they can comply or not comply. He said once that is done and it complies it will be sent to the Board or the Planning Commission. \par
\par
Mr. Ziskal said if they still do not comply they still have the opportunity to move forward. He said if staff finds it incompatible they must provide them with mitigation measures to make it compatible. He stated if they meet those requirements they would deem it compatible and move through the public hearings with their recommendation that it is compatible. He said if they do not meet those measures it will go through the public hearings and recommend denial based on compatibility. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said the Board makes a decision as a whole if it is compatible. He said if the applicant presents mitigation standards and the Board denies it they must explain in detail why the mitigation standards presented does not allow for compatibility. He said before we did not have to give specific reasons. He said once the Board makes a decision the avenue is Circuit Court to contest. He said it is a quasi-judicial hearing.\par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said we can still deny it and the question comes up is it a legally defensible denial. She said that is often where the public feels frustration when we approve what they consider to be non-compatible. She said with understanding the rules and regulations that guide them to the compatibility standard she believes this adds more objectivity to it and puts notice on them that if they deny it the successful legal challenge of an applicant is greater.\par
\par
Commissioner Braswell said these are the criteria, you approve it, or you are going to court. \par
\par
Commissioner Troutman said bills like this are coming down where they are losing home rule because the powers given to Planning Commissions and County Commissions across the state are not making decisions based upon Land Development Codes and the Comp Plan. She said this is the state saying we are going to continue ensuring that you are making the decisions as set forth. \par
\par
Mr. Mink said the CPA's are legislative whether they want that type of amendment. He said after that you get into the actual land use which is the Conditional Uses when their authority is less. He said when CPA's come through a lot of times that is the decision point. \par
\par
Chair Santiago said people see that we make the decision and all of the sudden it is turned around. She said that it is good that they talk about this and talk about it often. She said our hands are tied and the home rule is becoming even narrower everyday.\par
\par
The Chair opened a public hearing; no one spoke. \par
